papers.title: Query-Conditioned Evidential Keyframe Sampling for MLLM-Based Long-Form Video Understanding

venue.name: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)

papers.summary: An information-bottleneck formulation of keyframe selection that maximises query-conditional mutual information and decomposes the combinatorial search into efficient frame-level scoring, improving long-form video QA under tight token budgets.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: for two video questions, the frames scored most semantically relevant differ from the frames scored most evidential, with the evidence curve peaking inside the segment that actually answers the question

papers.title: Will My Assistant Remember My Allergy? What Personal LLM Assistants Forget When Conversation Memory Is Compressed
papers.summary: On PA-Bench, 100 assistant conversations we construct, a fact mentioned in passing survives compression to the question that needs it 0–1% of the time, against 97% with full memory. A compressed cache is an inference-reuse mechanism, not a persistence layer.
papers.summary_card: Benchmarks report that cache eviction keeps a fact like an allergy at a 20% budget — but they compress a prompt that already contains the user’s future question. Hide the question until after compression and the fact survives 0–1% of the time, against 97% with full memory. The cause is the budget, not the scorer.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: a user tells an assistant facts over several days, the assistant compresses its conversation memory, and days later either recalls the penicillin allergy or asks the user to state it again

papers.title: When No Answer Is Correct: Diagnosing Absent Answer Detection for MLLMs in Video Understanding

venue.name: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)

papers.summary: A diagnostic study showing that video MLLMs select plausible distractors instead of recognising when the correct answer is absent — a failure that worsens under temporal reasoning and resists prompting-based fixes.
papers.summary_card: When the correct answer simply isn’t among the options, video MLLMs pick a plausible distractor rather than abstaining. We show this failure worsens under temporal reasoning and resists prompting-based fixes.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: a viewer asks which symbol of the festival the video introduces, none of the three options is correct, and one model answers “B. Moose” while a reliable one answers “None of the above”

papers.title: Semantic-Unit Aggregation for Streaming Interaction Memory
papers.summary: A streaming-memory framework that organises interaction history by semantic unit rather than temporal window, retaining original events and improving long-horizon evidence retrieval.
papers.summary_card: Streaming memory is usually chopped into fixed temporal windows, which cuts events in half. We organise interaction history by semantic unit instead, keeping original events intact and improving evidence retrieval over long horizons.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: a verbatim interaction stream is aggregated into scene, belief and entity indexes, then queried twelve hours later

papers.title: Stable Scores, Unstable Answers: Frame Phase and Option Order in Video Multiple-Choice Evaluation
papers.summary: Benchmarks report the frame rate of a uniform sampling grid but not its phase. Two deployed samplers differing only by a half-step phase offset answer 23.6% of questions differently while scoring within a point. PhaseFusion averages the option posteriors of three offset grids and halves that instability.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: the same eight-frame budget read at two grid phases returns a wrong answer at one phase and the correct answer at the other

papers.title: Knowing When to Trust a Prior: Reliability-Gated Cue Fusion for Video Gaze Prediction
papers.summary: Gaze-free priors carry signal that gaze-trained models have not absorbed, if you know when to trust them. FocusGate reads three shape statistics of a defocus map per frame and lets the ensemble abstain, so rejected frames fall back to the base exactly. It improves all sixteen model-domain cells tested, for 1% added latency.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: eight gaze-free priors are rank-summed into a base prediction, and a reliability gate reading a defocus map decides per frame whether that map enters the sum

papers.title: Coupled but Late: Turn-Taking Between Full-Duplex Speech Models in Unscripted Dialogue
papers.summary: When two full-duplex speech models talk to each other, no human absorbs the timing error. Their turn-taking is genuinely coupled — re-pairing speakers destroys it — but the floor changes hands at a median of 400–560 ms against 137 ms for humans, consistent with waiting for the end rather than projecting it.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: two speech models exchange audio tokens on a shared clock, with 400 ms of mutual silence between one speaker finishing and the other answering

papers.title: StyleVAR: Controllable Image Style Transfer via Visual Autoregressive Modeling
papers.summary: A visual-autoregressive style-transfer framework that models VQ-VAE token sequences with a scale-dependent blended cross-attention to balance style and content, outperforming AdaIN across perceptual and structural metrics.

figure.alt: Figure from the paper: the StyleVAR architecture, where content and style token sequences enter an autoregressive transformer and its two attention branches are blended by a scale-dependent coefficient

papers.title: Hybrid Deep Learning for Credit Risk Prediction
papers.summary: An XGBoost–DNN stacking ensemble for loan-default prediction over 870,000+ records, with leak-proof cross-validation and SHAP-based interpretation.
